key_insight: GEAR shows that image tokenizers and autoregressive generators work better when they are trained together instead of separately. By aligning the tokenizer’s representations with what the generator can model easily, the system can produce more effective image synthesis.
problem_solved: Traditional visual generation pipelines train a tokenizer first and freeze it, which creates a mismatch between reconstruction quality and generation quality. This paper addresses the gap between what the tokenizer learns and what the generator actually needs.
method: Jointly train a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer and an autoregressive (AR) generator end-to-end.
Use representation alignment to guide the tokenizer toward latents that are easier for the generator to model.
Replace the standard two-stage training pipeline with a coupled optimization process for better synthesis performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, GEAR suggests a more efficient and better-aligned way to build generative image models. It can improve sample quality and training synergy by reducing the disconnect between compression and generation.

paper_title: GEAR: Guided End-to-End AutoRegression for Image Synthesis
paper_authors: Bin Lin, Zheyuan Liu, Chenguo Lin, Sixiang Chen, Yunyang Ge
